events.title: Leonardo da Vinci dies at Amboise
events.description: Leonardo died at Clos Lucé, the manor near Amboise given to him by Francis I. Painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, he also left thousands of pages of notes on anatomy, engineering and nature.
events.html: Leonardo died at Clos Lucé, the manor near Amboise given to him by Francis I. Painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, he also left thousands of pages of notes on anatomy, engineering and nature.

events.title: Anne Boleyn is arrested and taken to the Tower
events.description: Queen Anne Boleyn was arrested at Greenwich on charges of adultery, incest and treason. She was beheaded at the Tower seventeen days later, and Henry VIII married Jane Seymour within days.
events.html: Queen Anne Boleyn was arrested at Greenwich on charges of adultery, incest and treason. She was beheaded at the Tower seventeen days later, and Henry VIII married Jane Seymour within days.

events.title: Charles II charters the Hudson's Bay Company
events.description: The company received a monopoly of trade across the lands draining into Hudson Bay, a vast territory named Rupert's Land. It remains one of the oldest commercial enterprises in the world.
events.html: The company received a monopoly of trade across the lands draining into Hudson Bay, a vast territory named Rupert's Land. It remains one of the oldest commercial enterprises in the world.

events.title: Madrid rises against French occupation
events.description: Crowds in Madrid attacked French troops in the Dos de Mayo uprising, which was suppressed with mass executions painted by Goya. Revolt spread across Spain and began the Peninsular War.
events.html: Crowds in Madrid attacked French troops in the Dos de Mayo uprising, which was suppressed with mass executions painted by Goya. Revolt spread across Spain and began the Peninsular War.

events.title: Stonewall Jackson is shot by his own men at Chancellorsville
events.description: Returning from a night reconnaissance, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson was hit by fire from Confederate pickets. He died of pneumonia eight days later, a grave loss to Lee.
events.html: Returning from a night reconnaissance, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson was hit by fire from Confederate pickets. He died of pneumonia eight days later, a grave loss to Lee.

events.title: Berlin garrison surrenders to the Red Army
events.description: General Helmuth Weidling surrendered the German forces in Berlin to the Soviets two days after Hitler's suicide. Germany's unconditional surrender followed within a week.
events.html: General Helmuth Weidling surrendered the German forces in Berlin to the Soviets two days after Hitler's suicide. Germany's unconditional surrender followed within a week.

events.title: J. Edgar Hoover dies after 48 years leading the FBI
events.description: J. Edgar Hoover died in Washington, having led the Bureau and its predecessor since 1924. He built a modern federal police force but also used it to spy on activists and politicians.
